entities.name: Jean-Baptiste Francois des Marets, marquis de Maillebois
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jean-Baptiste François Desmarets, marquis de Maillebois (c. 1682 – February 7, 1762), rose to the rank of Marshal of France, distinguishing himself as a prominent military commander during the turbulent mid-18th century. His career spanned several major European conflicts, most notably the War of the Austrian Succession (1740–1748), where he commanded French forces in crucial theaters like Italy and the Low Countries. His strategic acumen, though sometimes criticized for its caution, played a significant role in shaping French military operations and diplomatic leverage during an era defined by dynastic rivalries and shifting alliances across Western Europe.

Maillebois began his military service during the War of the Spanish Succession, gaining early experience in complex campaigns. His command in Corsica from 1739 to 1740 effectively suppressed a rebellion, earning him a reputation for decisive action and administrative skill. However, it was during the War of the Austrian Succession that he achieved his greatest prominence. In 1741, he led a French army into Bohemia, though his subsequent command in Italy (1745–1746) proved more critical. There, he engaged Austrian and Sardinian forces, achieving mixed results but notably contributing to the French-Spanish efforts to secure influence in the Italian peninsula. His final major command placed him in charge of French forces in the Netherlands in 1747, where he participated in the strategic maneuvering against Anglo-Dutch-Austrian coalition armies.
